summary: charAt returns one UTF-16 code unit as a string at a zero-based index.
documentation: charAt returns one UTF-16 code unit as a string at a zero-based index. An out-of-range index returns an empty string instead of undefined. This makes a fixed-column character lookup easy to represent in JSON.
inputs: An object with text (ASCII string) and index (integer).
returns: One character, or an empty string for an out-of-range index.
caution: A Unicode character outside the BMP occupies two UTF-16 code units. This exercise uses ASCII so an index corresponds to one displayed character.
scenarios: Read a status flag from a fixed-width legacy record.
Extract one position from an ASCII product code.
Preview a selected character while teaching zero-based indexing.
title: Read a code position
problem: Input is {text, index}, where text contains only ASCII and index is an integer. Return the character at that index, or an empty string when index is negative or beyond the end.
goal: Use String.charAt() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: charAt supplies the empty-string fallback automatically.
